articles.headline: Cowboys' TD record: I caught a TD pass from Dak Prescott
articles.description: Prescott matched Tony Romo in the record book, so we sought the best moments from those who are helping him make history.
articles.body:
Editor's note: This story was originally published on Sept. 16. On Sunday, Dak Prescott tied Tony Romo for the most touchdown passes in Dallas Cowboys history by throwing three against the Washington Commanders.

FRISCO, Texas -- Sometime soon, perhaps as soon as Sunday against the Washington Commanders, Dak Prescott will set another Dallas Cowboys record: most touchdown passes in team history.

He has 245, leaving him three shy of the 248 Tony Romo threw from 2006 to 2016.

"I might remember every single one of them," Prescott said.

His first?

"Slant to Dez in the fourth quarter against Chicago," Prescott said.

True. Prescott's first touchdown pass was a 17-yarder to receiver Dez Bryant in the third game of his rookie season after being selected in Round 4 of the 2016 draft. The Cowboys beat the Chicago Bears, giving Prescott his first career victory at AT&T Stadium.

His favorite?

"I don't think I have a true favorite, one that stands out," Prescott said. "Any of them that have been a game winner or some big-time, fourth-quarter touchdowns, those are the ones that stick out in my mind."

Needing four touchdown passes against the Commanders in the Cowboys' home opener at AT&T Stadium on Sunday (4:25 p.m. ET, Fox) might seem daunting, but Prescott has already reached that mark four times against Washington, the last coming in a 38-10 win in Week 18 of the 2023 season.

Prescott has thrown touchdowns to 39 different players, including 10 current teammates. CeeDee Lamb has the most with 35. Eleven have caught one.

Instead of Prescott's favorite touchdown passes, ESPN asked nine current and former teammates to describe their favorite scoring receptions from the quarterback, including Lamb and right tackle Terence Steele, whose only career catch is a TD from Prescott.

CeeDee Lamb, WR

Situation: Week 17, 2023, vs. Detroit Lions, first quarter, third-and-13 from Cowboys' 8

Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes should have sacked Prescott, but somehow he escaped at the goal line, drifted to his right and let go of a deep ball toward Lamb. Before he caught the pass, cornerback Kindle Vildor fell. Lamb caught the ball at midfield and was able to jog into the end zone for a 92-yard score.

"Dak did a great job of beating the blitz. I did a good job of expanding on the scramble drill," Lamb said. "We preach extending drives and extending plays and that was a big part of that. That was one of the longest plays of my career. For sure, my most favorite."

It was the longest completion of Prescott's career, the longest catch of Lamb's and the second-longest completion in team history. It was also Lamb's 111th catch of the season, which tied him for Michael Irvin's team record for most in a season, which he later broke.

Has he ever run that far without being chased?

"Nah, I don't think I'll ever get that close to it again. Great time," Lamb said. "I enjoyed it. As you could tell, I trotted in the end zone. It was fire."

Jason Witten, TE

articles.headline: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
articles.body:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window (44 points) came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly WR Darius Cooper.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

CLE-TB | PHI-TEN | GB-NYJ

CIN-HOU | MIN-CHI | NO-BAL

CAR-ATL | PIT-NE

Catch up on Thursday's game:

DET-BUF

Cleveland 23, Tampa Bay 19

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Browns

What did Deshaun Watson do to earn another start? With rumblings that his starting job was on the line, Watson delivered arguably his best game in a Browns uniform. His performance was risk-averse, as Watson's 3.7 air yards per attempt were his fewest in a game as a Brown. But he made big plays in the second half, converting four third-down conversions on a go-ahead touchdown drive in the fourth quarter. It was the type of outing that Cleveland has been waiting for years to see.

Key stat to know: The Browns had scored fewer than 20 points in eight straight Watson starts entering Sunday's matchup. This was Cleveland's first time cracking 20-plus points in a Watson start since Week 10 of the 2023 season, a 33-31 win over the Ravens. -- Daniel Oyefusi

Next game: vs. Panthers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Buccaneers

Why have Baker Mayfield and the offense looked so out of sync? Mayfield just has not looked comfortable. The Bucs only found the end zone once -- in the third quarter with a 5-yard touchdown grab from Emeka Egbuka. The pair couldn't replicate this on fourth down with the game on the line after a lengthy weather delay. Mayfield also struggled to connect with Ted Hurst III (2-of-7 total and 1-of-4 on third down), including a 13-yard pass to the end zone he just couldn't hang onto in that final series. With the exception of a 49-yard dime to Tez Johnson, Mayfield struggled on the deep ball, where Mike Evans was always his most dependable weapon. He threw a first-quarter interception for his fourth turnover in two games.

Most surprising performance: No one has expected perfection, especially from a new piece navigating a new defense, but veteran linebacker Alex Anzalone has now surrendered eight receptions for 93 yards on eight targets -- along with a handful of missed tackles. articles.headline: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels suffers elbow injury against Cowboys
articles.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field in Sunday's game against the Cowboys after suffering an injured left elbow on the final play of the first half.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys after suffering an injured left elbow on the final play of the first half.

He was ruled out for the rest of the game. 

Daniels' feet appeared to get stepped on by left guard Chris Paul as the quarterback took the snap on a third-and-goal from the 1-yard line. Daniels started to fall down and tried to brace himself with his left elbow, which then bent back.

Daniels flung a pass attempt and stayed on the ground. He got up, started to run off the field then went back down to the ground. He was looked at by medical personnel and surrounded by a number of teammates as well as coaches, including Dan Quinn. As he was carted off, Daniels sat up with a towel over his head.

Daniels had dislocated his left elbow last season in Week 9 against Seattle. He returned four weeks later but reinjured the elbow attempting to make a tackle following an interception in Week 14 at Minnesota. He did not play the rest of the season.

On Sunday, Daniels had led the Commanders back from a 17-3 deficit by throwing a touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs and then leading them on a drive to end the first half. Washington decided to go for it on third-and-goal rather than kick a field goal with three seconds left.

Daniels completed 11 of 17 passes for 96 yards but hurt the Cowboys on the ground as well, resembling the player who was named the NFL's Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. Daniels had rushed seven times for 69 yards Sunday.

articles.headline: Deshaun Watson outplays Baker Mayfield, leading the Browns to a 23-19 win over the Buccaneers
articles.description: — Deshaun Watson earned at least a few more starts for the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — Deshaun Watson earned at least a few more starts for the Cleveland Browns.


              Watson threw two touchdown passes, including a go-ahead 17-yard toss to Blake Whiteheart in the fourth quarter, leading the Browns to a 23-19 comeback victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday in a game that was delayed two hours, 12 minutes because of lightning. 


              The Buccaneers (0-2) were driving and had a second-and-4 at the Cleveland 28 when the game was suspended at the two-minute warning. 


              When it finally resumed, heavy rain started falling again.


              Bucky Irving ran twice and Baker Mayfield's pass to Ted Hurst got the Bucs to the 13 before a holding penalty set them back. Mayfield's pass on fourth-and-10 from the 20 to Emeka Egbuka in the end zone was out of his reach, sealing the win for the Browns (1-1).


              Watson outplayed Mayfield on his home turf in the first meeting between two quarterbacks who are linked together. Watson was 24 of 30 for 238 yards with no turnovers and a 121.9 passer rating in his best game since Sept. 24, 2023 against Tennessee. 


              Mayfield, who was selected No. 1 overall by the Browns in 2018, was traded to Carolina after a blockbuster trade brought Watson and his off-field troubles to Cleveland in 2022. He was eventually released by the Panthers during that season and played for the Rams before rejuvenating his career in Tampa Bay, where he has made two Pro Bowls and received a $165 million, three-year contract extension earlier this month.


              Watson is 10-11 in five seasons with the Browns and seemed to be running out of time as a starter with Shedeur Sanders waiting to take over. But his performance against the Buccaneers should quiet critics for now and give first-year coach Todd Monken confidence to stick with him.


              Watson connected with Denzel Boston on a 55-yard TD pass to tie it at 16 late in the third quarter. Boston caught a slant, broke three tackles and sprinted into the end zone.


              Watson converted four times on third down on the drive that ended with his TD pass to Whiteheart that gave the Browns a 23-19 lead with 3:51 left in the game.


              Tampa Bay’s Chase McLaughlin and Cleveland’s Andre Szmyt combined to go 7-for-7 on field goals.


              McLaughlin connected from 59, 45, 31 and 31 yards. Szmyt was good from 50, 34 and 34 yards.


              Mayfield willed the Buccaneers into the end zone on the opening drive of the second half. He stiff-armed his way to a first down on third-and-9. On the next play, Mayfield eluded a sack, stepped up and threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to Egbuka, who had slipped and made the catch sitting on the ground.


              Mayfield threw one interception that Cleveland turned into three points.

articles.body:
Check out all of our starting pitcher rankings and other lineup selection tools here to help you make smart fantasy baseball lineup decisions. All fantasy advice is geared toward ESPN 10-team leagues with standard scoring.

Note: All information is accurate as of the time of publication. For updates, as well as any breaking news that might impact today's MLB slate, be sure to check out the latest fantasy baseball buzz. 

Other resources: RP depth chart | 2026 Rankings

ESPN's 2026 Player Rater | Betting notes for Monday

Pitchers to stream on Monday

Bailey Ober has walked an inordinately high number of hitters down the stretch. It's not the ideal setup for a streamer, but the Minnesota Twins have a road date with the San Francisco Giants so the veteran right-hander faces a depleted lineup in a pitcher's haven. The Giants will be without Rafael Devers for the rest of the season and may not have Bryce Eldridge come out of concussion protocol by game time.

Shane Baz left his last start after being struck on the elbow by a 105-mph line drive. He made it through the week unscathed, so he'll start for the Baltimore Orioles in the opener of a home series with the Toronto Blue Jays. On a busier slate, Baz would not make the cut, but there are only three games from which to choose, and the Blue Jays have struggled on the road facing right-handers all season.

Keider Montero will serve as the Detroit Tigers' primary pitcher when they host the Washington Nationals. River Ryan is set to make his Tigers debut, but he's probably earmarked for two or three frames before passing the baton to Montero. It should be a productive evening for the Tigers offense, giving Montero the chance for a win. He's had a couple of missteps over the past two months, but Montero has generally exhibited solid command and control this season, compensating for a low strikeout rate.

Hitters to stream on Monday

The Tigers' right-handed contingent lines up for a productive evening at Comerica Park with a matchup against Nationals lefty Jackson Kent. The southpaw sports a 6.40 ERA and 1.76 WHIP, fanning only 27 while walking a generous 23 in just 32 1/3 frames. Gleyber Torres, Hao-Yu Lee, Spencer Torkelson and John Peck enjoy the platoon advantage.

Brett Bateman hasn't compiled many homers and steals, but he gets on base and scores runs for the Toronto Blue Jays. He'll likely hit leadoff and enjoy the platoon edge with Shane Baz on the hill.

Walker Jenkins will be one of the favorites for next season's AL Rookie of the Year. The Twins are giving him a look down the stretch, and even though he's only hitting .211 through Saturday's action, he has clubbed three homers and a steal in his inaugural 18 games. The 21-year-old left-handed batter faces the San Francisco Giants' Landen Roupp. The right-hander sports a 1.77 ERA over his last four outings, but in 20 1/3 innings, he fanned only 13 while allowing 11 walks.

articles.headline: McCarthy takes blame for Steelers' offensive struggles in loss
articles.description: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy shouldered the blame Sunday in the wake of his offense's clunky, uninspired performance in a loss to the Patriots.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy shouldered the blame Sunday in the wake of his offense's clunky, uninspired performance in a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots.

"The reality of it is the detail's not there, and that's on coaching," McCarthy said. "Starts with me. I'm calling the offense. I have to get the detail better. So if you need someone, fire away because I felt it on Wednesday and Thursday. I'm a veteran coach. I know better, and I didn't do a good job.

"Offense needs to be better. Mike McCarthy needs to be better."

Not only did the Steelers offense put up just three points, but it has managed just one touchdown in 25 offensive possessions over the first two weeks of the season.

"It's frustrating, for sure," quarterback Aaron Rodgers said of not getting in the end zone. "The defense has been playing great. They've been holding [opponents to] 13 points a game in two games, and offensively I think we're averaging like eight points a game. That's not winning football."

Against the Patriots, the Steelers gained just 235 yards and averaged 3.5 yards per play. They went three-and-out on their first two drives and had four more in the second half. Their longest sustained drive (12 plays) ended in a disastrous third down on the doorstep of the red zone. Rodgers was drilled by linebacker Christian Elliss, fumbling as he was sacked. The ball bounced backward and was finally recovered by left tackle Troy Fautanu for a loss of 36 yards to bring up fourth-and-43.

"We just didn't get into a rhythm," Rodgers said of the offense. "We had too many three-and-outs again. I didn't feel like there was anybody that had an exceptional game out there. We all played below our standard."

Rodgers, who was replaced by backup quarterback Mason Rudolph with the game well out of reach in the final three minutes, completed 23 of 39 attempts for 187 yards.

Playing without receiver Michael Pittman Jr., the Steelers' pass game struggled to get going. Not only did Rodgers have an off-target percentage of 26%, his worst as a Steeler, but top receiver DK Metcalf was also held to two catches for 2 yards with two drops through the first three quarters.

"He's had a couple rough games, but he is one of the top receivers in the league for a reason," tight end Pat Freiermuth said of Metcalf. "And we back him every single day, and he's going to get out of it, man. He's a true pro's pro, and whatever he needs from us, everyone's already told him he's got it. So he'll be fine. He'll be bounced back next week, and can't wait. I mean, he's going to go out there the rest of the season and attack it, and he knows what went wrong and he's going to catch the ball."

articles.headline: Anderson tosses 7 shutout innings, Mariners beat Rockies 2-1 to avoid elimination
articles.description: — Rookie Kade Anderson tossed seven shutout innings, Dominic Canzone drove in two runs, and the Seattle Mariners beat the Colorado Rockies 2-1 on Sunday to stave off elimination from playoff contention.
articles.body:
DENVER -- — Rookie Kade Anderson tossed seven shutout innings, Dominic Canzone drove in two runs, and the Seattle Mariners beat the Colorado Rockies 2-1 on Sunday to stave off elimination from playoff contention.


              Anderson (2-2), in the longest of his six starts since making his major league debut Aug. 22 at the Chicago Cubs, followed his worst outing with his best. He gave up three hits, struck out a career-high seven and didn’t walk a batter.


              His performance kept Seattle’s slim postseason hopes alive. The Mariners (73-83) gained a game on Texas in the AL West and avoided, temporarily, being eliminated from the AL wild-card race.


              Mariners closer Andrés Muñoz left the game after walking TJ Rumfield with one out in the ninth. Muñoz bent over flexing his right arm after missing on a 98 mph fastball, bringing out the trainer. Manager Dan Wilson said Munoz’s issue was with his right knee He was replaced by Eduard Bazardo, who got the final two outs around a walk for his first save.


              Colorado catcher Hunter Goodman hit his 39th homer off Muñoz.


              Rockies starter Tomoyuki Sugano, who entered Sunday with a 7.41 ERA in three September starts, set down the first 10 batters before running into trouble in the fourth. He walked Randy Arozarena, and he scored from first on Canzone’s single to center.


              Canzone gave Seattle a 2-0 lead with an RBI double in the sixth off of Ryan Feltner.


              Colorado’s best scoring opportunity against Anderson was in the sixth inning when Jake McCarthy tripled with one out. Anderson got Connor Norby looking for the second out and struck out Goodman to end the inning.


              Rockies third baseman Kyle Karros was a late scratch with back spasms.


              Up next
              Mariners: RHP Logan Gilbert (12-10, 3.69 ERA) faces the Astros on Tuesday night to open the season-ending homestand.


              Rockies: LHP Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.38) opens the final home series against the Diamondbacks on Tuesday night.

articles.description: The Vikings should have QB Kyler Murray available to them next week. Murray is expected to clear concussion protocol "pretty early in the week," coach Kevin O'Connell said.
articles.headlineJa: QBカイラー・マレー（脳震盪）は第3週に復帰の見込み
articles.descriptionJa: バイキングスは来週、QBカイラー・マレーを起用できる見通しだ。ケビン・オコンネル監督によると、マレーは「週のかなり早い段階で」脳震盪プロトコルをクリアする見込みだという。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- After starting the season 2-0 behind backup quarterback Carson Wentz, the Minnesota Vikings should have starter Kyler Murray available to them next week. Murray is expected to clear concussion protocol "pretty early in the week," coach Kevin O'Connell said Sunday after the Vikings' 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears.

O'Connell did not announce that Murray would be the starter for the Vikings' next game, Sept. 27 at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but that has been the assumption around the team after Murray participated in all three practices last week on a limited basis.

"He's doing great," O'Connell said. "He's feeling well."

Murray suffered his concussion on the 11th play of his debut game with the Vikings last week, but his symptoms were minor enough to allow him to practice. Wentz has completed 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns since replacing Murray, without committing a turnover, and he made two throws in the fourth quarter Sunday that helped the Vikings drain clock while protecting a one-score lead.

Wentz hit receiver Jordan Addison on a 15-yard pass over the middle to convert a third down and later threw a 19-yard floater to tight end T.J. Hockenson on 2nd-and-10. Those completions helped the Vikings run 5 minutes, 8 seconds off the clock before taking a 6-point lead on Will Reichard's 39-yard field goal.

"It was ugly out there," Wentz said. "I'm not going to lie. But I'd rather win ugly than look good and come up with an 'L.'"

But there has never been any indication that Wentz has been playing his way into a full-time starting job. The Vikings' offense has finished with less than 300 total yards in both games this season, and Wentz has taken six sacks and had one interception overturned by a penalty. He had another likely interception dropped in Sunday's rainy conditions at Soldier Field.
